title: Prospective documentation of inpatient anthroposophic therapy approaches in pediatrics – acute bronchitis
summary: Acute bronchitis is one of the most common illnesses in children and one of the main reasons why they have to go to the doctor or hospital. Acute bronchitis is an inflammation of the bronchial tubes. Bronchitis is usually caused by viruses. Nevertheless, doctors often prescribe antibiotics. Antibiotics do not help with viral infections, so treatment is limited to the symptoms. Treatment from the field of integrative medicine could help the patient recover more quickly and feel better. Integrative medicine takes a holistic approach that considers the whole person. It combines conventional medicine with therapies from the fields of anthroposophic medicine and herbal medicine, among others.  In Germany, there are an increasing number of children's hospitals that offer integrative medical treatments in addition to standard therapy. Approximately 3,000 children are treated annually at the two anthroposophical certified clinics in Herdecke (Gemeinschaftskrankenhaus Herdecke)and Filderstadt (Filderklinik). Currently, there are few studies investigating these therapies. Many doctors, health insurance companies, and the general public therefore doubt the effectiveness of these therapies.  The objective of our study is to contribute to narrowing this gap. We want to find out how effective and safe the therapies are. We also want to find out how well the treatments can be implemented in everyday clinical practice by nursing staff and doctors. To this end, the course of the disease and the treatment are documented. There are also questionnaires for parents, doctors, and nursing staff.

interventions.name: Patients (aged 4 months to 17 years) who are admitted to the study center with acute bronchitis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis: Acute bronchitis (ICD J20, J20.0, J20.1, J20.2, J20.3, J20.4, J20.5, J20.6, J20.7, J20.8, J20.9)
- Sufficient knowledge of the German language
Exclusion criteria:
-Age: ≥18 years
-Lack of German language skills
